header.running_head: The Hospitality and service that the Ansaar Rendered

Hadhrat Abu Ayyoob (RA) then went to Basra where he stayed with Hadhrat Abdullaah bin Abbaas (RA). Hadhrat Abdullaah bin Abbaas (RA) emptied his home for Hadhrat Abu Ayyoob (RA) and said, "I shall do for you as you had done for Rasulullaah ﷺ." He then instructed his family to leave the house, which they did. Thereafter, he said to Hadhrat Abu Ayyoob (RA), "You may use anything in the house." In addition, he left with him forty thousand Dirhams and twenty slaves." [^1]

Another narration adds that Hadhrat Abu Ayyoob (RA) then went to Hadhrat Abdullaah bin Abbaas (RA) in Basra, who had been appointed as its governor by Hadhrat Ali (RA). Hadhrat Abdullaah bin Abbaas (RA) said, "O Abu Ayyoob! I wish to leave this house for you just as you left your house for Rasulullaah ﷺ." He then instructed his family to leave, which they did. Thereafter, he gave everything in the house to Hadhrat Abu Ayyoob (RA). When Hadhrat Abu Ayyoob (RA) was leaving the place, Hadhrat Abdullaah bin Abbaas (RA) asked him, "How much do you need?" Hadhrat Abu Ayyoob (RA) told him that he required the amount that he usually received as a grant and eight slaves to work in his fields. His grant was four thousand Dirhams, so Hadhrat Abdullaah bin Abbaas (RA) gave him five times the amount, which was a sum of twenty thousand Dirhams and forty slaves. [^2]
Hadhrat Abdullaah bin Abbaas (RA) Goes out of his Way to Have the Needs of the Ansaar Fulfilled

Hadhrat Hassaan bin Thaabit (RA) narrates that they were a group of the Ansaar who needed to place a request before the Ameerul Mu'mineen who was either Hadhrat Umar (RA) or Hadhrat Uthmaan (RA)[^3]. They proceeded with Hadhrat Abdullaah bin Abbaas (RA) and a group of other Sahabah (RA). Hadhrat Abdullaah bin Abbaas (RA) and the other Sahabah (RA) all spoke to the Ameerul Mu'mineen and mentioned the virtues of the Ansaar. However, the Ameerul Mu'mineen had to make an excuse. The need of the Ansaar was an urgent one and the Sahabah (RA) repeated the request several times. However, they all eventually accepted the excuse and just stood there. Not Hadhrat Abdullaah bin Abbaas (RA). He persisted and said, "Never! By Allaah! (I shall never accept the excuse because) Then the Ansaar will have no status. They assisted Rasulullaah ﷺ and granted him protection."
Rooyaani and Ibn Asaakir, as quoted in Kanzul Ummaal (Vol.7 Pg.95). Haakim has also reported the narration from reliable sources as confirmed by Dhahabi.

Tabraani, as quoted in Majma'uz Zawaa'id (Vol.9 Pg.323). Haythami has commented on the chain of narrators. Haakim (Vol.3 Pg.461) has also reported the narration with an extended chain of narrators and commentary.
One of the narrators by the name of Ibn Abi Zinaad was unsure about who the Ameerul Mu'mineen was during that time.
